title: Ordering nodal branches makes their vertical ideals agree generically on overlaps
statement:
Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-weil-field, def-kun-separably-closed], and $V\subseteq K$ a valuation ring with fraction field $K$, meaning that $a$ or $a^{-1}$ lies in $V$ for every $a\in K^\times$. Assume that its primes form a finite chain, and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $X$ be an affine flat finitely presented $S$-scheme with pure one-dimensional geometric fibres [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-weil-pure-dimension]. Assume that every nonsmooth geometric fibre point has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Assume that each reduced irreducible component of each fibre $X_s$ is smooth over $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-irreducible-components, lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme, def-weil-residue-field]. Fix an affine scheme $Y$, etale $S$-morphisms $p:Y\to X$ and $h:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}V[u,v]/(uv-c)$ with $0\ne c\in V$ [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-polynomial-ring], and a point $y\in Y$ such that $x=p(y)$ is nonsmooth and $u(h(y))=v(h(y))=0$. There exist affine Zariski opens $x\in U\subseteq X$ and $y\in Y_0\subseteq p^{-1}(U)$ such that $p_0:Y_0\to U$ is surjective. Put $W=Y_0\times_UY_0$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $r_1,r_2$, and denote the restricted coordinate functions $h^*u,h^*v$ on $Y_0$ by $u_0,v_0$. For every $s\in S$ and generic point $\xi$ of every irreducible component of $W_s$, one has
$$(r_1^*u_0)\mathcal O_{W,\xi}=(r_2^*u_0)\mathcal O_{W,\xi},\qquad (r_1^*v_0)\mathcal O_{W,\xi}=(r_2^*v_0)\mathcal O_{W,\xi}.$$
No descent of these ideals to $U$, or etale map from $U$ to a standard nodal model, is asserted.

source.place: Agent reconstruction of the branch-comparison subargument after Tag 0CBY, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family. The tag supplies the initial etale charts only. The finite-height all-fibres smooth-component ordering assertion is additional, not quoted as the statement of 0CBY. Temkin Section 4.3, printed p.27, supplies motivation only (its smooth-component observation there is over a field).

proof.text: Write $s_0$ for the image of $y$ in $S$. The generizations of $s_0$ form an affine open: if there is a next larger prime, choose $a$ in it but not in $s_0$, and $D(a)$ consists exactly of the primes contained in $s_0$; otherwise take $a=1$. Its ring is $R=V_{s_0}$. Replace $X,Y$ by their inverse images over this open, still affine, retaining $x,y$. These replacements are allowed since the requested opens lie inside them. Throughout the argument etale maps stay etale under base change and open restriction by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits, lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Both charts, and all the affine branch schemes below, are of finite presentation over their affine targets by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Thus their fibres over fields are finite type. The spectrum of $R$ is a finite chain with closed point $s_0$.

source.place: Agent reconstruction of the ordered-branch comparison after Tag 0CBY, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family; the chart is already a hypothesis.

proof.text: For each prime $\mathfrak t\subseteq R$ containing $c$, put $A_{\mathfrak t}=R/\mathfrak t$ and form the closed subschemes $B_{\mathfrak t,u}=V_Y(\mathfrak t,u)$ and $B_{\mathfrak t,v}=V_Y(\mathfrak t,v)$. They are etale respectively over $\operatorname{Spec}A_{\mathfrak t}[v]$ and $\operatorname{Spec}A_{\mathfrak t}[u]$, by base change of $h$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. The ring $A_{\mathfrak t}$ is a valuation domain: for nonzero residues $\bar b,\bar d$, apply the valuation alternative to $b/d$ in $\operatorname{Frac}R$ and reduce the resulting relation $b=ed$ or $d=eb$ modulo $\mathfrak t$. This gives one of $\bar b/\bar d,\bar d/\bar b$ in $A_{\mathfrak t}$. It is normal by [lem-weil-pbc-valuation-ring-normal]; its one-variable polynomial rings are normal domains by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-normal-domain]. Their localizations at primes are normal domains by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain], so these polynomial rings are normal rings in the local sense required below. Consequently both $B_{\mathfrak t,u}$ and $B_{\mathfrak t,v}$ are normal by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-over-normal-ring-normal]. They contain $y$.

source.place: Agent reconstruction of the ordered-branch comparison after Tag 0CBY, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family; the chart is already a hypothesis.

proof.text: Each branch scheme in Step 2 has Noetherian underlying space. Indeed its base $\operatorname{Spec}A_{\mathfrak t}$ has finitely many points, and each fibre is finite type over a field, hence a Noetherian scheme by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], i.e. a finite union of affine opens with Noetherian rings, each of which has Noetherian underlying space by [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space]; so each fibre has Noetherian underlying space by the finite-union argument of the next sentence. A descending chain of closed sets stabilizes on each fibre and therefore on their finite union. By [lem-trf-normal-topologically-noetherian-components], each branch scheme has finitely many disjoint closed and open normal integral components. Retain its unique component containing $y$ and remove all its other components from $Y$. Those other components are closed in the branch scheme, hence closed in $Y$, and avoid $y$. There are finitely many $\mathfrak t$ and two choices of branch, so all these removals leave an open neighbourhood of $y$. Take an affine open $Y_1$ inside it containing $y$. For every $\mathfrak t$ containing $c$, both $V_{Y_1}(\mathfrak t,u)$ and $V_{Y_1}(\mathfrak t,v)$ are nonempty open subschemes of their retained normal integral components; in particular they are integral.

source.place: Agent reconstruction of the ordered-branch comparison after Tag 0CBY, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family; the chart is already a hypothesis.

proof.text: The closed subscheme $N=V_{Y_1}(u,v)$ is etale over $\operatorname{Spec}R/(c)$, by base change of $h$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. Its image is open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open, def-weil-etale-morphism] and contains the closed point $s_0$. An open of a local spectrum containing its closed point is the entire spectrum: it contains a basic open $D(b)$ with $b$ outside the maximal ideal, and such $b$ is a unit. Thus $N_{\mathfrak t}$ is nonempty for every $\mathfrak t$ containing $c$. Choose a point $z_{\mathfrak t}$ of it. No finiteness or section theorem for $N$ is needed.

source.place: Agent reconstruction of the ordered-branch comparison after Tag 0CBY, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family; the chart is already a hypothesis.

proof.text: Fix such $\mathfrak t$. Each integral affine branch scheme $V_{Y_1}(\mathfrak t,u)$ or $V_{Y_1}(\mathfrak t,v)$ is flat over $A_{\mathfrak t}$, since it is etale over its polynomial line. For flatness of the composite one can identify successive tensors: an injection stays injective first after tensoring with the free polynomial module (the identification $M\otimes_A A[T]=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}M$ makes the induced injection coefficientwise) and then after tensoring with the flat etale algebra [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Its section ring $H$ is a domain, and $A_{\mathfrak t}\to H$ is injective: for $0\ne b\in A_{\mathfrak t}$ flat tensor injectivity makes multiplication by $b$ injective on the nonzero ring $H$, so its image cannot be zero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-generic-fibre-localization-domain-irreducible] to identify the generic fibre over $\mathfrak t$ with the spectrum of a domain. Hence $C_u=V_{(Y_1)_{\mathfrak t}}(u)$ and $C_v=V_{(Y_1)_{\mathfrak t}}(v)$ are integral. They are nonempty by Step 4.

source.place: Agent reconstruction of the ordered-branch comparison after Tag 0CBY, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family; the chart is already a hypothesis.

proof.text: The two integral curves $C_u,C_v$ cover $(Y_1)_{\mathfrak t}$, since $uv=0$ on that fibre. Both contain $z_{\mathfrak t}$. Each is etale over its affine line. Its open image contains $0$ and therefore also points outside $0$ [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Thus $v$ is nonzero on $C_u$ and $u$ is nonzero on $C_v$, so neither is contained in the other. They are exactly the two irreducible components. The fibre is reduced by [etale-proposition-etale-reduced], since $\kappa(\mathfrak t)[u,v]/(uv)$ embeds into $\kappa(\mathfrak t)[u]\oplus\kappa(\mathfrak t)[v]$ by evaluation at $v=0,u=0$, whose kernel calculation is $(u)\cap(v)=(uv)$ in the polynomial ring. Moreover $z_{\mathfrak t}$ is nonsmooth. The origin of the standard fibre is not formally smooth: the map $u,v\mapsto\epsilon$ to $k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$, $k=\kappa(\mathfrak t)$, cannot lift to $k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^3)$, as any two lifts have product $\epsilon^2\ne0$. This obstruction also lies in every open neighbourhood of the origin, since the test schemes have a single point. By [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] the origin is nonsmooth, and [lem-trf-etale-source-smoothness] reflects this through $h_{\mathfrak t}$ at $z_{\mathfrak t}$.

source.place: Agent reconstruction of the ordered-branch comparison after Tag 0CBY, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family; the chart is already a hypothesis.

proof.text: The open map $p_{\mathfrak t}:(Y_1)_{\mathfrak t}\to X_{\mathfrak t}$ sends the generic points of $C_u,C_v$ to generic points of irreducible components $D_u,D_v$ of $X_{\mathfrak t}$. Here is the topological argument, used again below. In a space with finitely many irreducible components, remove all components other than a chosen one; the remainder contains a nonempty open in that component. Its image under an open map is a nonempty open in the target and lies in the irreducible closure of the image of the chosen component. This closure must be a whole target component, since a proper irreducible closed subset of a component cannot contain a nonempty open of the target. The image of a generic point is generic for that closure by continuity. The fibres here are Noetherian, so [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components] gives the required finiteness. Openness is [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open, def-weil-etale-morphism].

source.place: Agent reconstruction of the ordered-branch comparison after Tag 0CBY, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family; the chart is already a hypothesis.

proof.text: The components $D_u,D_v$ are distinct. Otherwise write $D$ for their common reduced component; it is smooth by the hypothesis on $X$. Every section of its ideal pulls back to zero on each integral $C_u,C_v$: it is zero at the component generic point, and a domain injects into its fraction field. It therefore pulls back to zero on $(Y_1)_{\mathfrak t}$. For this last implication explicitly tensor the injection $k[u,v]/(uv)\hookrightarrow k[u]\oplus k[v]$ of Step 6 with the flat etale algebra of $(Y_1)_{\mathfrak t}$, using [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine, lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact, def-weil-etale-morphism]. This yields an injection of that algebra into its two branch quotients. Thus $p_{\mathfrak t}$ factors scheme-theoretically through $D$, and this factor is etale: its base change along $D\hookrightarrow X_{\mathfrak t}$ is itself [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. Composition with the smooth $D\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ makes $(Y_1)_{\mathfrak t}$ smooth. This uses etale-implies-smooth [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres] and affine smooth comparison and composition [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine, lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition], locally on $D$. It contradicts Step 6 at $z_{\mathfrak t}$.

source.place: Agent reconstruction of the ordered-branch comparison after Tag 0CBY, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family; the chart is already a hypothesis.

proof.text: The image $p(Y_1)$ is open and contains $x$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Choose a principal affine open $x\in U\subseteq p(Y_1)$ of the affine $X$, say $U=D(f)$. Put $Y_0=Y_1\cap p^{-1}(U)=D(p^*f)$; this is affine and contains $y$, and $p_0:Y_0\to U$ is surjective by the choice of $U$. The component and distinct-image conclusions of Steps 5--8 persist: the two branch fibres are replaced by nonempty open subsets (they still contain the points of $N$ over the local base after the final restriction, since $y$ is retained and Step 4 applies again), and their generic images remain the distinct $D_u,D_v$ restricted to $U$.

source.place: Agent reconstruction of the ordered-branch comparison after Tag 0CBY, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family; the chart is already a hypothesis.

proof.text: Form $W=Y_0\times_UY_0$. Each projection is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]; so are its fibre maps. They are open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open, def-weil-etale-morphism]. The scheme $W$ is affine ($U$ is affine) and of finite presentation over the base, so each $W_s$ is finite type over $\kappa(s)$ and, exactly as in Step 3, has Noetherian underlying space [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian, lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space], hence finitely many irreducible components [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components]. Let $\xi$ be a component generic point of $W_s$. Applying the open-map argument of Step 7, each $r_i(\xi)$ is a component generic point of $(Y_0)_s$. If $c\in\mathfrak p_s$, the two points must lie on the same labelled branch: otherwise their images under $p_0r_1=p_0r_2$ would be the two distinct generic points of $D_u\cap U,D_v\cap U$. Thus either both pulled-back $u$ coordinates are units at $\xi$, or both pulled-back $v$ coordinates are units there. If $c\notin\mathfrak p_s$, all four coordinates are units since their pairwise products equal the base unit $c$. Points outside the chosen base open have empty fibre and impose no condition.

source.place: Agent reconstruction of the ordered-branch comparison after Tag 0CBY, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family; the chart is already a hypothesis.

proof.text: Work now in the local ring $\mathcal O_{W,\xi}$. A coordinate nonzero at the corresponding fibre generic point has nonzero residue and hence is a unit in this local ring. If the two $v$ coordinates are units, the identities $(r_i^*u_0)(r_i^*v_0)=c$ give $(r_i^*u_0)=(c)$ and $(r_i^*v_0)=(1)$ for $i=1,2$. If instead both $u$ coordinates are units, the same identities give $(r_i^*u_0)=(1)$ and $(r_i^*v_0)=(c)$. When $c$ is a unit all four ideals are $(1)$. These are precisely both asserted equalities. This calculation establishes only the fibre-generic ideal comparisons claimed here.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q19-836b7299e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, its 11 steps, the new node, every cited node statement, the parent strict-chart Step 3 that applies the item, the unit sk-i-curve-zero with its transitive route, and Stacks 0357 (properties.tex lemma-normal-locally-finite-nr-irreducibles) and 0052 (topology.tex lemma-Noetherian). The statement is unchanged and true, and it is not an nt-target, so no base-change morphism or coefficient category is involved. Test cases: the standard chart uv=c, c a unit on a generization, a disconnected chart. Dropping the smooth-component hypothesis lets a self-nodal component break the conclusion, so that hypothesis is genuinely needed, and Step 8 is where it is used. Steps 1, 2, 4-9 and 11 are correct as written. Step 2 is correct: R/t is a valuation domain, normal, the polynomial ring and its localizations are normal, and an etale extension of a normal ring is normal. Step 4: the open image in local Spec R/(c) is everything. Step 5: flat over a domain gives an injective map, and the generic-fibre localization is a domain. Step 6: the eps^3 obstruction plus pointwise etale reflection. Step 8: at the generic point the ideal is nilpotent, so it pulls back to zero in the domains; flat-tensor injectivity gives scheme-theoretic factorization through the smooth component, and etale plus smooth makes the fibre smooth, a contradiction. The new node lem-trf-normal-topologically-noetherian-components is true (0357 with 0052(1),(2)) and stated alone without a proof, as required. It is not a duplicate: rem-pc-regular-normal (2) and lem-fin-etale-normal-components need algebraic Noetherianity, which fails for valuation-base branch schemes.
